# Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL — facts

> Source-anchored units about Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL: 33 across 13 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-06 · 33 units · 13 sources · rights: quote -->

## How it works

- [statement] On Jupiter Perps JLP markets (SOL, ETH, wBTC), liquidation triggers when the oracle price crosses the liquidation price and the protocol takes all remaining collateral as the liquidation fee, so the trader gets nothing back. On Beta markets remaining collateral after loss and fees is returned to the trader. The Beta markets run on a separate engine that does not feed the JLP pool. The JLP pool is the counterparty, so trader profits are paid from the pool. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/liquidation · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/earn/jlp/faq
- [statement] Drift's insurance fund also tops up a perp market's P&L pool, which is not a bankruptcy. resolve_perp_pnl_deficit pays only when the AMM's total fee minus distributions is negative, the P&L pool holds less than users' net P&L, and net unsettled P&L exceeds the market's configured unrealized_pnl_max_imbalance. The payment is the smallest of that excess, the market's remaining per-period revenue-withdraw allowance, its remaining tier claim, and the vault balance minus 1 token. Neodyme describes the same instruction. (high confidence) — https://github.com/drift-labs/protocol-v2/blob/master/programs/drift/src/controller/insurance.rs · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://neodyme.io/reports/Drift.pdf, https://github.com/drift-labs/protocol-v2/blob/master/programs/drift/src/state/perp_market.rs
- [statement] Bullet's docs describe a USDC insurance fund that covers a shortfall when liquidation fails, then ADL as the last line: traders are ranked by leverage and unrealized P&L, and profitable high-leverage positions are reduced. The docs claim this avoids socialized loss. A banner says Bullet is replacing ADL with 'social deleverage (SDL)' and an updated page is coming. A backstop liquidator vault takes over failing positions at the bankruptcy price. The pages carry no date. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.bullet.xyz/exchange/trading/insurance-fund-and-adl · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://docs.bullet.xyz/exchange/trading/liquidation
- [statement] The Insurance Fund also pays through a second path that is not a bankruptcy: resolve_perp_pnl_deficit. It moves quote tokens from the fund into a perp market's P&L pool only when the AMM is underwater (total_fee_minus_distributions below zero), the P&L pool is smaller than net user P&L, and net unsettled P&L exceeds the market's unrealized_pnl_max_imbalance. The draw is the smallest of the excess imbalance, the remaining per-period withdrawal allowance, the remaining lifetime insurance cap, and the vault balance minus one token. Velocity's docs say this draw covers a P&L deficit, not funding, and that no path runs from the revenue pool to a perp AMM. (high confidence) — https://github.com/drift-labs/protocol-v2/blob/master/programs/drift/src/controller/insurance.rs · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/how-it-works/revenue-pool, https://neodyme.io/reports/Drift.pdf
- [statement] A Velocity spot bankruptcy draws first on the bad-debt market's own revenue pool, which is first-loss capital. It then draws on that market's Insurance Fund vault, always leaving at least one token. Last, it cuts the deposit-interest index for every lender in that market, never below 1. Perp bankruptcies must resolve before spot ones, because both draw on the same quote vault. A spot resolution fails with PerpBankruptcyMustPrecedeSpot while a cross-margin perp bankruptcy is unresolved. (high confidence) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/risk-and-safety/liquidation-and-bankruptcy · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://github.com/velocity-exchange/velocity-v1/blob/master/programs/velocity/src/controller/liquidation.rs

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] To judge a Velocity market's real cover, read the contract tier before the market. Velocity's Risks page says insurance coverage, oracle tolerance, TWAP damping, auction bands and the AMM cutoff all derive from the tier, and that a re-tier changes the insurance cap, confidence tolerance, TWAP band and auction band at once. Routine changes are timelocked, the most dangerous need the cold key, and a cold-tier change carries no notice period. Live values sit in each market account, not in the docs. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/risk-and-safety/risks · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/risk-and-safety/contract-tiers

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Velocity's liquidation engine uses an unbuffered entry test at the maintenance requirement and a 2% of notional exit buffer above maintenance. Margin shortfalls under $50 free immediately, and positions of $50 or less can be taken in full. Liquidation is rejected with PriceBandsBreached when oracle and 5-minute TWAP diverge by 50% or more. Liquidator, insurance-fund and protocol fees are admin-set per market, initialize to zero, and the docs show 0.75% liquidator and 0.75% insurance-fund fees only as an example. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/liquidations/liquidation-engine · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL
- [statement] Jupiter's liquidation price formula uses a 500x protocol-level max leverage to set minimum maintenance margin, although the trading maximum is 250x. Accrued borrow fees shift the liquidation price toward the market price over time. If fees exceed collateral minus size/500, a position can be liquidated with no adverse price move. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/liquidation · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL
- [statement] Jupiter's Beta markets run on a separate engine (GUM) with USDC collateral and do not use the JLP pool. A forced close fills on the orderbook, a liquidation fee of 0.75% to 1% applies, and leftover collateral returns to the trader, though in a fast market it can be little or nothing. Jupiter's docs state: 'There is no auto-deleveraging on Beta markets at launch.' (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/beta-markets · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/faq
- [statement] Zeta's retired platform funded its insurance fund from all platform fees, a fixed share of liquidation incentives and an initial seed. The liquidation reward was 65% of maintenance margin, 30% to the liquidator and 35% to the fund. The fund paid when no liquidator stepped in or a liquidated account could not pay the reward. If liquidation and the fund both failed, an over-bankruptcy ratio on withdrawals, AB x DP/(DP+BA), shared the loss across depositors. The Zeta Foundation says the platform was sunset in May 2025, and the docs pages carry no date. (medium confidence) — https://docs.zeta.markets/zeta-protocol/exchange-architecture/margin-system/liquidations-and-insurance · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://docs.zeta.markets/zeta-protocol/exchange-architecture/margin-system/liquidations-and-insurance/insurance-fund, https://docs.zeta.markets/zeta-protocol/exchange-architecture/margin-system/liquidations-and-insurance/socialized-loss, https://zeta-foundation.gitbook.io/zeta-foundation/winding-down-zex
- [statement] Velocity's liquidator fee ages. After a 600-second grace period from liquidation entry, it rises by 0.01 bps every 400 ms. The cap is the lesser of three times the base liquidator fee and the market's maintenance margin ratio. The default exit buffer is 2% of notional. Liquidator, insurance-fund and protocol fees are admin-set per market, and the docs say all three initialize to zero. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/liquidations/liquidation-engine · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://github.com/velocity-exchange/velocity-v1/blob/master/programs/velocity/src/math/constants.rs, https://github.com/velocity-exchange/velocity-v1/blob/master/programs/velocity/src/math/liquidation.rs
- [statement] Two streams feed a Velocity Insurance Fund. First, perp trading fees, liquidation fees and borrow fees land in the spot market's revenue pool, and a permissionless settle moves a capped slice into the fund vault, by default every 3,600 seconds. Each settle is capped at one tenth of the revenue pool and at a 1000% annualized rate on the smaller of the live vault balance and the lowest balance since the last settle; both caps are skipped while the fund has no stakers. Second, a fraction of deposit-interest gains goes straight to the fund. Spot trading adds nothing. The per-liquidation insurance fee is credited to the liability market's revenue pool. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/insurance-fund · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/insurance-fund/insurance-fund-staking, https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/how-it-works/revenue-pool, https://github.com/velocity-exchange/velocity-v1/blob/master/programs/velocity/src/controller/insurance.rs
- [statement] Velocity liquidation starts when total collateral falls below the maintenance requirement; the entry test has no buffer. The engine cancels open orders first and re-runs the margin check. It then transfers only enough position to reach the maintenance requirement plus a 2% of notional buffer (DEFAULT_LIQUIDATION_MARGIN_BUFFER_RATIO). A throttle caps the first fill at an admin-set initial percentage of the shortage and ramps to 100% over an admin-set duration. A shortage under $50 frees at once, and a position of $50 or less can be taken in full. The transfer price is the oracle price, and liquidation is rejected with PriceBandsBreached when the oracle and the 5-minute TWAP differ by 50% or more. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/liquidations/liquidation-engine · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/risk-and-safety/risks, https://github.com/velocity-exchange/velocity-v1/blob/master/programs/velocity/src/math/constants.rs
- [statement] Drift-lineage and Zeta liquidations are permissionless position transfers to third-party liquidators, not forced sales into the book. On Velocity the liquidator takes the position at the oracle price and must meet the initial margin requirement of what it takes on. Zeta's liquidator trades with the liquidatee at Zeta's stored mark price. Zeta sets the reward at 65% of the liquidatee's maintenance margin, 30% to the liquidator and 35% to the insurance fund. (medium confidence) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/liquidations/liquidation-engine · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://docs.zeta.markets/zeta-protocol/exchange-architecture/margin-system/liquidations-and-insurance
- [statement] Jupiter's Beta markets (JUP, HYPE, ZEC and stock perps) run on GUM, an orderbook engine separate from the JLP pool. Liquidation triggers at the mark price, and the forced close fills on the orderbook. Whatever collateral remains after loss and fees goes back to the trader, which can be little or nothing in a fast market. The liquidation fee is 0.75% on crypto markets and 1% on stock markets. A position above its first margin tier is liquidated one tier at a time. The docs say 'There is no auto-deleveraging on Beta markets at launch' and describe no insurance fund. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/beta-markets · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/faq

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Drift's insurance fund is a staker-funded backstop meant to keep the exchange solvent when liquidations or borrower defaults leave collateral insufficient. Staking is a risk position, not a deposit: the stakers' principal is what absorbs bad debt. (medium confidence) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/insurance-fund · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://www.drift.trade/updates/incident-recovery-update-april-16-2026-now
- [statement] ADL is a last-resort loss-socialization mechanism: when liquidations fail to keep the exchange solvent, profitable positions are forcibly reduced to cover the deficit. Gauntlet's paper argues an ADL policy faces a trilemma among exchange solvency, revenue and trader fairness, and that moral hazard grows with participation so zero-loss socialization is impossible. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2512.01112v2 · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://thogiti.github.io/2025/12/11/Autodeleveraging-Hyperliquid-653M-debate.html
- [statement] On the JLP markets, liquidation triggers when the oracle price reaches the position's liquidation price, with no margin call. The protocol takes all remaining collateral as the liquidation fee, after the loss, close fee and borrow fees, so the trader gets nothing back. The formula uses an internal 500x limit for minimum maintenance margin, although 250x is the trading maximum. Accrued borrow fees move the liquidation price toward the market price over time. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/liquidation · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/faq
- [statement] Anyone can resolve a latched bankruptcy in Velocity. A solvency flag, separate from the withdraw pauses and flipped only by the cold-admin key, gates resolution. Perp bankruptcies must resolve before spot ones (error PerpBankruptcyMustPrecedeSpot) because both draw the same quote insurance vault. The code comment says a caller-chosen order would shift loss between perp stakers and spot depositors, and credits audit finding #52. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/risk-and-safety/liquidation-and-bankruptcy · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://github.com/velocity-exchange/velocity-v1/blob/master/programs/velocity/src/controller/liquidation.rs
- [statement] Velocity keeps a standing first-loss tranche so a permissionless fee sweep cannot drain it. Each market holds back a floor of its in-transit insurance fee, by default 0.1% of open-interest notional priced at the oracle TWAP. When a bankruptcy latches, the sweep withholds the whole in-transit fee, and delisting is blocked until the claim clears. On a market with $50,000,000 of open interest the default floor is $50,000. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/risk-and-safety/liquidation-and-bankruptcy · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://github.com/velocity-exchange/velocity-v1/blob/master/programs/velocity/src/math/constants.rs
- [statement] Unstaking from an Insurance Fund takes at least 13 days. The default cooldown is set per spot market, and legacy Drift v2 has the same THIRTEEN_DAY default. A request freezes the share value. At completion the payout is the smaller of the frozen value and the current value, so gains after the request do not reach the staker but a bankruptcy draw during the cooldown does. Neodyme describes the same smaller-of rule. Completion also fails while the spot market's utilization or its TWAP is above 90%. Request and completion both fail with ExchangePaused when withdrawals are paused exchange-wide. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/insurance-fund/insurance-fund-staking · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://github.com/drift-labs/protocol-v2/blob/master/programs/drift/src/math/constants.rs, https://neodyme.io/reports/Drift.pdf
- [statement] Zeta's documented backstop had three layers. A liquidator takes the position. The insurance fund, made of platform fees, a fixed share of liquidation incentives and an initial seed, pays when no liquidator steps in or the liquidated account cannot fund the reward. If both fail, the over-bankruptcy loss is shared across all depositors by scaling withdrawals by DP/(DP+BA), where DP is deposits to the platform and BA is the bankruptcy amount. The Zeta Foundation page says Zeta Protocol would cease operations in May 2025, so this is a historical design. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.zeta.markets/zeta-protocol/exchange-architecture/margin-system/liquidations-and-insurance · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://docs.zeta.markets/zeta-protocol/exchange-architecture/margin-system/liquidations-and-insurance/insurance-fund, https://docs.zeta.markets/zeta-protocol/exchange-architecture/margin-system/liquidations-and-insurance/socialized-loss, https://zeta-foundation.gitbook.io/zeta-foundation
- [statement] On Jupiter's JLP markets (SOL, ETH, wBTC) the JLP pool is the counterparty to every trade. When traders profit the pool pays out, and when traders lose the losses flow back into the pool. Jupiter's April 2026 collateral assessment calls this 'the defining risk of JLP' and says JLP holders absorb losses during sustained trader profits. The JLP virtual price is the pool's asset value net of the value reserved to pay traders' profits. (high confidence) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/earn/jlp/faq, https://static-r2.jup.ag/lend/risk-research/jlp-risk-report.pdf
- [statement] Auto-deleveraging (ADL) is a last-resort loss-socialization mechanism for perpetual futures venues. It runs when liquidations fail to keep the venue solvent and other loss-absorbing resources, such as the insurance fund, cannot cover the shortfall. The venue then forcibly reduces the positions of solvent traders on the other side, at prices that leave the venue solvent. Two separate research groups give this definition: Gauntlet's Tarun Chitra and a Columbia University team. (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01112v3 · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.15963v1

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Drift is characterized as using pro-rata loss allocation rather than a ranked ADL queue. The Gauntlet paper treats pro-rata as the fairest rule. Dan Robinson's critique, summarized in a blog, says Drift's version allocates by contract size, whereas the paper's pro-rata model is equity-based. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2512.01112v2 · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://thogiti.github.io/2025/12/11/Autodeleveraging-Hyperliquid-653M-debate.html
- [statement] The Hyperliquid ADL critique turned on units. Dan Robinson argued, per a secondary blog summary, that Hyperliquid's ADL closes contracts rather than taking each winner's whole equity, and that Drift's pro-rata rule allocates by contract size while the paper's rule is equity-based. Chitra's v3 concedes both: it adds a Corrections section and says Drift implements contracts-pro-rata, which should not be conflated with its wealth-pro-rata benchmark. Hyperliquid's Jeff Yan replied that ADL 'has nothing to do with HLP or backstop liquidations' and that ADLs net made users hundreds of millions by closing profitable shorts at favorable prices. (medium confidence) — https://thogiti.github.io/2025/12/11/Autodeleveraging-Hyperliquid-653M-debate.html · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://protos.com/outdated-algorithm-caused-650m-excess-losses-on-hyperliquid-report, https://arxiv.org/html/2512.01112v3

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Velocity's bad-debt waterfall for a perp market runs in this order: the liquidated account's estate (remaining deposit and P&L-pool claims), the market's in-transit insurance fee, the insurance fund up to the market's tier cap, the AMM fee-provision clawback, then socialization. Socialization spreads the residual across surviving open interest in that perp market through both cumulative funding rates. Spot shortfalls instead cut the deposit-interest index across depositors. Winning positions are not exempt. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/insurance-fund · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL
- [statement] Per the Gauntlet paper, BitMEX ranked ADL candidates by profit times leverage starting in 2016, Binance used the same formula from 2019, and Hyperliquid uses a queue derived from Huobi's 2015 design. The paper says queue-based methods are the worst policies for the top winning trade. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2512.01112v2 · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL
- [statement] In Velocity, only tiers A, B and C draw on the shared insurance fund. A Speculative, Highly Speculative or Isolated market draws nothing, and a new market starts at Highly Speculative until an admin promotes it. Bad debt in a zero-cover market goes to the estate, the market's in-transit insurance fee, the AMM fee-provision clawback, and then to that market's own traders. An admin can re-tier a market under an open position, which changes its insurance cap at once. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/risk-and-safety/contract-tiers · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/risk-and-safety/liquidation-and-bankruptcy, https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/risk-and-safety/risks
- [statement] Both Drift-lineage codebases socialize a perp residual by dividing it by the market's total open base (absolute long base plus absolute short base), adding the result to the long cumulative funding rate and subtracting it from the short rate. Every open position pays per unit of base, once, whatever its side or profit, and no position is closed. Drift's docs say the same: 'paid for pro-rata (by base amount) by all open positions'. A spot residual instead lowers the deposit interest index, a pro-rata haircut to every lender in that market. (high confidence) — https://github.com/drift-labs/protocol-v2/blob/master/programs/drift/src/math/liquidation.rs · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/risk-and-safety/liquidation-and-bankruptcy, https://web.archive.org/web/20260209075253/https://docs.drift.trade/protocol/insurance-fund, https://thogiti.github.io/2025/12/11/Autodeleveraging-Hyperliquid-653M-debate.html
- [statement] Each spot market has its own insurance fund, held in that market's asset. The quote-asset fund backs every perp. Stakers hold shares. To unstake, a staker requests, waits (13 days by default, set per spot market), then withdraws. The payout uses the lower of the share price at request and at withdrawal. A draw after the request therefore reaches the staker and a gain does not. (high confidence) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/insurance-fund · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/insurance-fund/insurance-fund-staking, https://neodyme.io/reports/Drift.pdf, https://github.com/drift-labs/protocol-v2/blob/master/programs/drift/src/math/constants.rs
- [statement] Both codebases socialize the last residual with a cumulative funding-rate bump, not by closing positions. calculate_funding_rate_deltas_to_resolve_bankruptcy divides the residual loss, rounded up, by total open base, which is the absolute long base plus the absolute short base. The program adds that delta to the long cumulative funding rate and subtracts it from the short rate, so longs and shorts both owe the same amount per unit of base, once, at resolution. The call fails with CantResolvePerpBankruptcy if total open base is zero. Velocity's docs give an example: a $2,000,000 residual over 100,000 SOL long and 100,000 SOL short costs $10 per SOL. (high confidence) — https://github.com/drift-labs/protocol-v2/blob/master/programs/drift/src/math/liquidation.rs · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL · also: https://github.com/velocity-exchange/velocity-v1/blob/master/programs/velocity/src/math/liquidation.rs, https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/risk-and-safety/liquidation-and-bankruptcy
- [statement] Velocity bankruptcy resolution is permissionless: anyone may resolve a latched perp or spot bankruptcy. A solvency flag, separate from the general withdraw pauses and flippable only by the cold-admin key, gates it. An admin can therefore pause withdrawals without blocking bad-debt resolution. Only the Velocity docs state this; the instruction code was not checked for the flag. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/risk-and-safety/liquidation-and-bankruptcy · keywords: Liquidation engines insurance funds and ADL
